description: How a client converts a major-1 drama into major 2 (doc/protocol.md, section 7). Normative data: the client applies it as written and knows no major-1 record format beyond it. Every path is project-relative; {object} is a v1 object id with its version segment removed, {owner} the object a record stage belongs to, {file} a path inside a version folder.

version_folders.a_version_folder_is: a folder holding records_in_a_version_folder.version_record whose name matches one of version_folder_name_patterns

paid_call_settled.note: a paid call is settled when its paid_call record's field is one of states: its output downloaded, not charged (rejected, failed, expired, cancelled), or counted as charged with its output gone (lost). Any other state, succeeded included, is still owed by its provider or of unknown outcome; once Pine runs the major-2 tools nothing settles it, so the conversion converts as found and names each such version (doc/protocol.md 7, Freeze).

writes.{owner}/entry.json: entry.json without entry_json_drop_fields and without the description field (description_field_by_owner_kind); every other field (look, members, establishing, …) stays, until a character's look and a prop's text move into its description.md, after the person's pending text (pending_text): the one-editable-text merge (doc/protocol.md 2.2)

inside_of.why: a scene's inside_of names a key prop (a vehicle) or an exterior scene (a building), as drama-cli's plan.outside_stage resolves it, props first

appears_in.value: a list of episode ids, one relation per item

writes.{owner}/description.md.receipt.json: the receipt rule below, from this describe version's job.json, only when {owner}'s current entry version was written from this call: its artifact.json metadata has source.kind "describe" and source.call naming this describe version. A description the person wrote later (entry describe) has no receipt.

record_stages.receipt_when_note: each key is a dot path into the metadata of the artifact.json of {owner}'s current entry version; <this version> is this describe version's folder, {object}/<version id>

every_other_version.copies: each file records_in_a_version_folder.outputs_and_metadata lists under outputs, at {object}/{file}, except what skip_folders_in_version and skip_files_in_version name; input/ is copied, which keeps bible/input/brief.md and bible/input/screenplay.md
every_other_version.also_copies_note: a key matches a v1 object id, * standing for one path segment; technical-check.json is written after artifact.json, so artifact.json does not list it

skip_outputs_by_object.note: a scene node's copies of its views are not copied: each view is its own scene_view object (pictures_that_become_objects)

receipt_rule.beside: each file the current version copies (outputs), as <file>.receipt.json

fields.inputs_sent_in_order: version.json inputs in order, each {path: the input version's shown file at its major-2 path, sha256: that file's hash}; an input whose version has no shown file is left out
fields.cost: {usd: job.json actual_usd, reported_by: "pine" when job.json connection is set, otherwise job.json provider}; null when actual_usd is null

not_version_folders.config/<v>/drama-cli.cfg.yaml: the newest is written to drama-cli.cfg.yaml at the root
not_version_folders.turns/: dropped (kept in the backup); read first for the snapshots above
not_version_folders.choices.json: dropped (kept in the backup); read first for current, discarded and the person's pending text

newest_version_to_root.copied_as_it_is: drama-cli drops an old config's project key itself when it reads one (its migrated_config, D329), so the conversion copies the file unchanged

not_version_folders.dropped_wherever_they_are_note: folders of these names, at any depth (the root, an episode, a variant): drama-cli's own records of major 1, its understand calls, its asset-library uploads and its stored prompts, since every prompt is composed when drawn (doc/protocol.md 2.2); drama-cli of major 2 keeps such records in pine-computer-records/ and reads none of these (kept in the backup)

current.rule: each kept object's files are the files of its major-1 current version (major 1's 3.2: the chosen version, else the newest not discarded), and every object.json is written (see object_json); earlier versions are kept in the backup only, and the converted folder is recorded as one commit, authored client-found-changes-on-disk
current.removed_objects: an object choices.json marks removed is deleted, with every variant under it
current.pending_text: choices.json description becomes {object}/description.md; its prompt is dropped (kept in the backup), since every prompt is composed when drawn

read_from: when the folder has no turns/: the major-1 client's own records of that drama (for Pine Drama Studio, returns/<task>.json in its storage), the same installed snapshots
snapshots.when_neither_exists: the conversion refuses, changes nothing, and asks the person to open the project once in the previous client (major 1), which writes turns/, with a link to its download
snapshots.an_object_is_kept_when: the latest installed snapshot of its scope lists it (the Project Chat's for shared objects and episode objects, a snapshot listing its episode for an episode's objects), as major 1's 5.3 has it; an object it no longer lists is deleted

object_json.written_for: every object the kept snapshots list, every asset or variant with an entry stage, and every folder that pictures_that_become_objects names

one_source_per_field.type, name, setting, variant_of, relatio: from the object's current entry version when it has an entry stage (record_stages /entry), otherwise from the latest snapshot that lists it (type, name, segment; relations from its edges inside_of and appears_in; a needs edge is dropped, since nothing in major 2 writes or reads it; variant_of from its edge variant_of)
one_source_per_field.shown_file: the version.json file of the object's current version
one_source_per_field.objects_sent_by_draw_request: the current version's version.json inputs, in order, keeping only inputs whose version has a shown file (the pictures the draw sent), each mapped to its object id; for a planned object with no version: the inputs of the latest snapshot that lists it, in order. Absent when the list would be empty.

object_json.written_in: describing each object's current version, and every object without one

pictures_that_become_objects.note: a key matches a major-1 object folder, * standing for one path segment; <the character's name>, <the scene's name> and <the variant's name> are the owner's object.json name, and <side> is the last path segment; shown_file and objects_sent_by_draw_request follow object_json's rules like any object
